requirement: Tracy's mail and the pages around it say what the code does: one sign-in code lifetime, no promised reply mail, a staff invitation with its link, HTML bodies delivered, and a Morgan contact form that mails only the site administrator

oracle.ref: PR #844 (fix); fix evidence: Issue #794 (QA audit, re-verified on develop f9c734938). On base 811108bd2 the same three runs are red by assertion: web 25 of 63 (one of them only because the base still answers 405 to a signed-in GET of the join page, which #843 made 200), Morgan 32 of 39, gateway 1 of 3. On the earlier wording of this branch ('If you already have a code … it still works until it expires') the eight rate-limit tests are red by assertion, 8 of 63: a first code replaced by a second one met every stated condition and was still rejected. The login page said 'a few minutes', the mail '10 minutes', the lane page 'one hour'; four send sites passed {to, subject, text} and dropped the built HTML; the staff invitation named no address; the Morgan handler called wp_mail a second time with the posted address when contact_email_copy was set, and died with a TypeError on a non-string field.
oracle.invariant: All three runs exit 0 with 0 failures and 0 skipped tests. 'F-S1-005: the login page, the local preview and the mail all state CODE_TTL_MS' passes: in each of the eight languages the code step of /login, the local preview note, the sign-in mail's text, HTML and preheader print CODE_TTL_MS in minutes and leave no {minutes} unfilled. 'F-S1-005: the rate-limit sentence is the restricted one, stored whole in each of the eight languages' and 'F-S1-005: every consumer of the rate-limit sentence prints the restricted text' pass: the form answer, the first-request and resend branches of the page script and the exported English message all print exactly 'Too many sign-in codes were asked for. Try again later.' (or its translation), with no slot and no number — nothing about an earlier code, its lifetime or a waiting time. The six 'F-S1-005 state matrix: …' tests pass, each in all eight languages over the real memory store and the real limiter: an inbox never mailed a code, a code used up by wrong tries, a code already used, a code past its lifetime, a code replaced by 'Send a new code', and a latest valid code. In every state the request over the cap answers 429 (page) and 429 RATE_LIMITED (JSON), mails nothing and leaves the code table as it was; the used-up, used, expired and replaced codes are rejected with 401 afterwards, and the latest valid code still signs in with 303. 'the code page states no lifetime of its own, in any of the eight languages' passes for the lane gateway: no hour, no minute, no number; English and Chinese are written out, and 'the six catalogue files hold no unsourced translation of it: those languages read the English sentence' passes (no existing catalogue translates the sentence, so it stays a listed English fallback). 'F-S1-006: the "request sent" page makes no promise of a reply by mail, in any language' passes, and so does 'F-S1-006: reopening the join page shows what the note says: waiting, approved, and nothing for a declined request': the note promises no visible answer, an approved request shows the access page, a declined one shows the request form. 'every mail that carries a link refuses an address that does not parse, and keeps one that does' and 'F-S1-010: an origin that makes an unopenable link mails nothing and answers 202 notified:false' pass. 'F-S1-010 + F-S1-017: inviting Tracy staff mails the /ops/invite link, HTML and text' passes for an invitee with and without an account: the provider payload carries <origin>/ops/invite/<workspace id> in text and as an href. The three link tests pass: signed out redirects to /login?next=<the link>; the invited account accepts its own pending grant and lands on /ops; another account gets the 'no longer open' page and the UPDATE is only ever for the caller's own account id. The four 'F-S1-017: … with the HTML the builder wrote' tests pass: team invitation, join request (every admin), staff invitation and removal code reach the provider payload with html equal to the builder's html; a provider rejection keeps notified:false / 201 / 202 / 502 MAIL_NOT_SENT as before. For both overlays/ and src/ of wp-ja-morgan: '"send me a copy" selects no recipient, however it is posted' passes (exactly one message, to admin_email); the honeypot, field, nonce and administrator-address tests refuse before wp_mail with no PHP warning; 'one client address sends 5 an hour; the next is refused' passes; forwarding headers do not change the bucket; a store that cannot be written refuses the message; a failed wp_mail is reported as error-send; 'a request left over from the hour before cannot clear or reopen this hour’s places' passes for the Contact and Quick Contact handlers. Not covered by this case: PostgreSQL (the database is a fixture that answers listed statements only), a real browser or mail client, a real mail provider, WordPress itself and its database (stubbed functions; add_option's real insert, the clean-up DELETE on MySQL, PHP's clock and two concurrent requests are not exercised), what a reverse proxy puts in REMOTE_ADDR, and the mail palette (F-S1-025, not changed).
